name: Rebamipide
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Rebamipide is a gastric mucosal protectant; about 10% of a dose appears in urine. In kidney impairment, single-dose levels are higher and the half-life longer, but the Japanese insert reports no accumulation with repeated dosing in dialysis patients and sets no kidney dose change. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The Japanese insert describes kidney impairment and dialysis without numeric thresholds or dose changes; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 100 mg three times daily (morning, evening and at bedtime for gastric ulcer) (PMDA insert).

The Japanese insert gives no dose change and has no kidney-impairment caution section (no section 9.2). Levels were higher and the half-life longer after a single 100 mg dose in kidney impairment; steady-state levels in dialysis patients matched single-dose predictions, so no accumulation is expected (PMDA insert 16.6.1).

monitoring: Liver tests and blood counts if symptoms (hepatic dysfunction, jaundice, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia reported); stop if marked transaminase rise with fever and rash (PMDA insert).
